cases.reviewerAnswer: Use the imperfecto to present repeated past actions as habits, without presenting their beginning or end as the focus.
cases.notes: The rule appropriately distinguishes contextual clues from automatic tense selectors.

cases.reviewerAnswer: Temporal cuando is unaccented; interrogative cuándo takes a written accent.
cases.notes: The qualification «Питальне» makes the distinction accurate. Interrogative cuándo also occurs in indirect questions.

cases.reviewerAnswer: Identify past habits and circumstances from short recordings; treat dictation as a separate optional activity.
Interpret the expressions in their past context and make pequeño/niño agree with the person described.
de niño/de niña means in childhood, with gender agreement.
de pequeño/de pequeña means as a child or when young, with gender agreement.
en aquella época means at that time or in those days.
entonces can mean then/at that time or so/therefore.
pueblo is masculine, plural pueblos; here it means a village or small town.
cases.notes: The cultural note is appropriately qualified with «часто».

cases.reviewerAnswer: Describe former routines with the habitual imperfecto and distinguish them from present routines and completed episodes. Temporal cuando is unaccented; interrogative cuándo is accented.
cases.element: content.body.steps[0].blocks[5].text: «Cuando без знака наголосу — «коли» в розповіді; у питанні пишемо ¿cuándo?»
cases.defect: The wording makes sentence type determine the accent. Temporal cuando remains unaccented inside a question, as in ¿Qué hacías cuando eras pequeño? Interrogative cuándo also takes an accent inside a declarative sentence, as in No sé cuándo llegó.
cases.correction: Distinguish temporal cuando from interrogative cuándo by function. Explain that question marks or declarative sentence form alone do not determine the accent.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, treatment of «cuando/cuándo» and direct versus indirect interrogation (from memory).
Course contract, rule 8.
cases.notes: The example Cuando era pequeño, vivía en un pueblo is correct.

cases.reviewerAnswer: trabajaba is the neutral background reading; trabajé also fits a completed former employment stage.
cases.element: task.prompt[1].text: «Antes ___ en un banco, pero ahora trabajo en casa. (trabajar, yo)»; task.errors[e1]: «trabajé».
cases.defect: The contrast between former and current employment does not uniquely determine aspect. Antes trabajé en un banco, pero ahora trabajo en casa is natural when the former employment is presented as a completed stage. The prompt does not specify the intended viewpoint.
cases.correction: Specify that the speaker is describing the usual situation during the former period, or review both aspectual readings instead of categorically rejecting trabajé.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 23, perfective and imperfective presentation of past situations (from memory).
Packet verdict instructions: use uncertain when the key selects one of several contextually possible readings.

cases.reviewerAnswer: iba for a descriptive childhood routine; fue is possible when the repeated visits are summarized as a completed series.
cases.element: context.taughtBefore omits the irregular imperfect of ir required by task.prompt[1].text: «De pequeña, Lucía ___ al parque todos los días. (ir)»; task.errors[e1].feedbackUk: «Fue подає дію як одну завершену подію.»
cases.defect: The required form iba is not established by the mapped singular regular imperfect prerequisites or explained in a teaching hint. In addition, fue does not necessarily denote one occurrence: todos los días can describe repeated visits presented collectively as completed.
cases.correction: Document prior teaching of iba. Clarify the intended habitual viewpoint or review fue as an alternative reading, and replace the single-occurrence explanation with an accurate explanation of perfective aspect.
sources: Course contract, rule 1; this case's context.taughtBefore lists regular singular imperfect forms but no imperfecto.ir.
RAE, Diccionario de la lengua española, «ir», conjugation table: imperfect indicative iba (from memory).
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 23, perfective aspect and repeated past events (from memory).
cases.notes: The aspectual choice is underdetermined independently of the definite prerequisite and feedback defects.

cases.reviewerAnswer: cenaban for a former routine; cenaron permits a completed-episode reading of antes.
cases.element: context.taughtBefore lists only singular imperfect forms, while task.prompt[1] requires cenaban; task.errors[e1].feedbackUk: «Cenaron — одна завершена подія.»
cases.defect: Producing the third-person plural imperfect requires a form not documented in the prerequisite map. The feedback also treats cenaron as necessarily one occurrence, although the preterite can summarize a completed series. The sentence does not explicitly fix a habitual rather than episodic reading.
cases.correction: Document prior instruction in plural -ar imperfect forms. Clarify the intended routine and revise the feedback to distinguish aspectual presentation without equating the preterite with one occurrence.
sources: Course contract, rule 1; context.taughtBefore names imperfecto.regular-ar.singular but no plural imperfect instruction.
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 23, imperfective and perfective past readings (from memory).

cases.reviewerAnswer: jugaba is the neutral habitual reading; jugó is also possible as a retrospective summary of childhood.
cases.element: task.prompt[1].text: «De niño, mi hermano siempre ___ con su perro. (jugar)»; task.errors[e1]: «jugó».
cases.defect: De niño and siempre establish a childhood pattern but do not uniquely require imperfective aspect. Siempre jugó can summarize a pattern throughout a completed childhood period. The prompt does not specify which presentation is intended.
cases.correction: Specify the descriptive habitual viewpoint, or review both jugaba and jugó with explanations of their different aspectual presentations.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 23, habitual and iterative readings with imperfective and perfective past forms (from memory).

cases.reviewerAnswer: leíamos for the former habit; leímos is possible when the earlier reading activity is presented as completed.
cases.element: context.taughtBefore lists singular -er/-ir imperfect forms, while task.prompt[1].text «Antes nosotros ___ mucho, pero ahora no tenemos tiempo. (leer)» requires leíamos.
cases.defect: The task requires production of the first-person plural imperfect, but the prerequisite map establishes only singular forms. The rule hint explains tense use without teaching the plural ending.
cases.correction: Document prior teaching of plural -er/-ir imperfect forms or use a singular subject. Also clarify the intended habitual viewpoint before categorically rejecting leímos.
sources: Course contract, rule 1; context.taughtBefore names imperfecto.regular-er-ir.singular but no plural imperfect instruction.
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 23, aspectual presentation of past situations (from memory).
cases.notes: The antes/ahora contrast alone does not exclude a completed earlier period.

cases.reviewerAnswer: iba for a descriptive childhood habit; fui can summarize the repeated summer visits as a completed series.
cases.element: context.taughtBefore omits imperfecto.ir; task.prompt[1].text: «De pequeño, yo ___ a casa de mis abuelos todos los veranos. (ir)».
cases.defect: The assessed production requires irregular iba, which is absent from the mapped prerequisites and is not taught by the rule hint.
cases.correction: Document earlier teaching of iba or replace ir with a taught regular verb. Clarify the intended aspectual viewpoint or review fui rather than rejecting it solely because the visits recur.
sources: Course contract, rule 1; this case's context.taughtBefore.

cases.reviewerAnswer: tomabas for a former habit; tomaste or has tomado can fit an earlier episode, depending on its time frame.
cases.element: task.prompt[1].text: «Antes tú ___ mucho café y ahora no tomas nada. (tomar)»; task.errors[e1–e3].
cases.defect: Antes can mean formerly or earlier on a particular occasion. Ahora no tomas nada can likewise describe a current habit or current behaviour. The task does not establish which temporal scale is intended, so its categorical rejection of episodic past forms is not secure.
cases.correction: Supply a former habitual period and identify the statement as a description of that routine, or review the episodic readings separately.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario de la lengua española, «antes», temporal senses (from memory).

cases.notes: The choice between tomaste and has tomado additionally depends on the episodic time frame.

cases.reviewerAnswer: empezaba for the usual schedule; empecé can refer to a particular starting occasion while salía supplies a usual or planned finishing time.
cases.element: task.prompt[1].text: «En mi antiguo trabajo, ___ a las ocho y salía a las tres. (empezar, yo)»; task.errors[e1]: «empecé».
cases.defect: The routine reading is the most natural, but the sentence does not explicitly say that both times describe a recurring schedule. A particular start followed by an imperfect background or planned departure is another possible reading. Coordination with salía does not itself require matching aspect.
cases.correction: Specify that the speaker is describing the usual daily schedule, rather than a particular starting occasion.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 23, combinations of perfective events with imperfective background and prospective imperfect uses (from memory).

items.reviewerAnswer: c for a descriptive former routine; a is also possible as a completed series of weekends.
items.notes: The feedback contains a definite false simplification independently of the contextual uncertainty.
